Commands lab

Type /. Pick a contract. Get evidence back.

Practice cutting AI slop with VS Code chat slash commands: built-ins such as /plan, /compact, and /disableAutoApprove, plus 12 custom commands shipped as prompt files.

Open the Command Studio Read the lab guide Command reference
  • 43 commands: 31 built-in, 12 prompt files
  • 8 exercises with real checks
  • 6 GIF walkthroughs
  • 14 slop smells in Mission mode

Start in five steps

You need Node.js 22.20+ and VS Code with GitHub Copilot Chat in agent mode, allowed by your organization. The guide, the studio, and the exercises need no npm install.

Get the starter code, checks, hints, and reference solutions from the GitHub repository, or download and extract the ZIP. GitHub Pages hosts the demos; real exercises run locally.

git clone https://github.com/AkashAi7/anti-ai-slop.git
cd anti-ai-slop/commands

Already cloned? Open the commands folder in your existing copy. ZIP downloads extract to anti-ai-slop-main; open its commands folder instead.

  1. In VS Code, use File > Open Folder and open the downloaded commands folder, not its parent. VS Code loads the custom commands from .github/prompts only when this folder is the workspace root. Run the following commands in that folder's integrated terminal.
  2. Open the Command Studio. It runs offline from a local file.
    npm.cmd run studio
  3. Start the terminal guide, choose 01-clarify-before-code, then run setup, baseline, and prompt.
    npm.cmd run demo
  4. In the Chat view, set the Session Target to Local and use agent mode. Type / and /clarify appears next to the built-ins. Paste the prompt and answer the agent's questions in your own words.
  5. Check your work.
    npm.cmd run check -- 01-clarify-before-code

On shells other than PowerShell, use npm in place of npm.cmd.

The Command Studio

An interactive single page that runs offline. It makes no network requests and sends nothing to a model. Open a mode directly:

ModeWhat you do
1 WatchStep through or play the 5 walkthroughs. These are the scenes the GIFs are recorded from.
2 Try itA simulated chat box. Type / to open the palette, then press Tab to fill in a command and Enter to send it. Custom commands show their real prompt file and a scripted sample answer.
3 Mission14 slop smells. Pick the command that fixes each one, then read why.
4 CommandsSearch and filter all 43 commands by mechanism and kind.

Commands by mechanism

The 12 lab commands are prompt files in .github/prompts, and each one declares only the tools its job needs. The 31 built-ins ship with VS Code chat. Registry as of 2026-10-30.

What the access classes mean
read-only
Reads and searches only. Cannot edit files or run commands.
runs-commands
Runs terminal commands (each still needs your approval). Cannot edit files.
writes-artifact
Writes one named Markdown artifact. Instructed not to touch code.
edits-code
Edits code and runs tests. Keep approvals on.

Showing 43 of 43 commands.

No commands match these filters.

Plan Decide before code.

Slop smell: Code arrives before anyone agreed what done means. Assumptions stay silent.

  • /clarifyLab commandread-only

    Surface ambiguities and silent assumptions before any code is written. Asks at most 5 questions.

    Slop it targets
    Silent assumptions baked into code.
    Evidence you get back
    At most 5 questions, each with a reason and a proposed default, plus an assumptions table. No code.

    Read the prompt file: /clarify

  • /specLab commandread-only

    Turn an agreed request into a short, testable spec with acceptance criteria and real verification commands.

    Slop it targets
    "Done" that nobody can test.
    Evidence you get back
    Goal, non-goals, Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, edge cases, and real verification commands. Undecided items marked OPEN.

    Read the prompt file: /spec

  • /planBuilt-in

    Research and propose an implementation plan.

    Puts a reviewable plan in front of you before any edit, while wrong assumptions are still cheap to fix.

    Example: /plan add expiry checks to discount codes; list open questions first
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /plan

  • /explainBuilt-in

    Explain code.

    Builds an accurate picture of existing behavior before you ask for a change.

    Example: /explain how applyDiscounts treats unknown codes
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /explain

Ground Anchor every claim in repo truth.

Slop smell: Invented helpers, guessed config keys, and packages nobody checked.

  • /groundLab commandread-only

    Map what a change needs to what already exists in the repo, with file:line evidence. Flags invented helpers, config keys, and APIs.

    Slop it targets
    Invented helpers, config keys, and APIs.
    Evidence you get back
    A Need / Status / Evidence table with file:line for every EXISTS or SIMILAR row.

    Read the prompt file: /ground

  • /deps-checkLab commandread-only

    Verify every import, package, and API member against the manifest, the standard library, or official docs. Never installs anything.

    Slop it targets
    Hallucinated packages, invented API members, and trivial dependencies.
    Evidence you get back
    An Import / Kind / API / Verdict table. Anything unverifiable is marked UNVERIFIED. Nothing is installed.

    Read the prompt file: /deps-check

  • /initBuilt-in

    Generate or update workspace instructions in a local agent session.

    Records real build, test, and layout conventions so every session starts grounded.

    Example: /init
    Where: Local agent session · VS Code docs for /init

  • /instructionsBuilt-in

    Configure instruction files.

    Shows which standing rules the agent receives, so you can fix stale ones.

    Example: /instructions
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /instructions

  • /create-instructionsBuilt-in

    Generate an instructions file in a local agent session.

    Turns a correction you keep repeating into a rule the agent always sees.

    Example: /create-instructions money is integer cents; never use floats
    Where: Local agent session · VS Code docs for /create-instructions

Verify Evidence, not claims.

Slop smell: "All tests pass" with no command output, tests that cannot fail, and symptom patches.

  • /deslopLab commandread-only

    Review a change for AI-slop patterns (swallowed errors, fake tests, duplicate helpers, debug prints, narrating comments) and report findings only.

    Slop it targets
    Swallowed errors, fake tests, duplicate helpers, debug prints, and narrating comments.
    Evidence you get back
    A findings table with file:line, pattern, why it matters, and the smallest fix. No edits.

    Read the prompt file: /deslop

  • /verifyLab commandruns-commands

    Run the real checks and report only what was observed - command, exit code, result. Ends with VERIFIED or NOT VERIFIED.

    Slop it targets
    "Should work" and "all tests pass" with no evidence.
    Evidence you get back
    Command, exit code, and observed result for every check, then claims vs evidence, then VERIFIED or NOT VERIFIED.

    Read the prompt file: /verify

  • /root-causeLab commandruns-commands

    Reproduce a bug, test at most 3 hypotheses, and confirm the root cause before any fix. Rejects special-casing the reported input.

    Slop it targets
    Special-casing the reported input instead of fixing the defect.
    Evidence you get back
    A reproduction, at most 3 hypotheses, the confirmed cause, and a proposed fix plus regression tests. No edits.

    Read the prompt file: /root-cause

  • /fail-pathsLab commandedits-code

    Enumerate edge cases and failure paths, write tests for them, and run them. Never weakens an assertion to get green.

    Slop it targets
    Happy-path-only tests.
    Evidence you get back
    An edge-case table, new tests, and the observed test run. Assertions are never weakened.

    Read the prompt file: /fail-paths

  • /fixBuilt-in

    Suggest a fix for a problem in your code.

    Aims the agent at one concrete problem instead of an open-ended rewrite. Follow it with /verify.

    Example: /fix the failing expiry test
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /fix

  • /testsBuilt-in

    Generate tests.

    Gets tests written early. Review every assertion: a test that cannot fail proves nothing.

    Example: /tests for parseDuration, including malformed input
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /tests

  • /setupTestsBuilt-in

    Get help choosing and setting up a test framework (experimental).

    A repo without a test runner cannot produce evidence. Fix that first.

    Example: /setupTests
    Where: Local - experimental · VS Code docs for /setupTests

Contain Limit the blast radius.

Slop smell: A one-line fix rewrites five files, changes a public API, or edits frozen code.

  • /scopeLab commandwrites-artifact

    Write SCOPE.md - a short contract of allowed changes, forbidden paths, frozen API, done-when, and rollback - before any edit.

    Slop it targets
    Scope creep and drive-by edits.
    Evidence you get back
    A SCOPE.md of at most 40 lines: allowed changes, forbidden paths, frozen API, done-when, and rollback.

    Read the prompt file: /scope

  • /simplifyLab commandedits-code

    Remove duplication, dead code, and speculative abstraction without changing behavior. Tests must be green before and after.

    Slop it targets
    Speculative abstraction and duplicate code.
    Evidence you get back
    Tests green before and after, with a list of each removal and why behavior is unchanged.

    Read the prompt file: /simplify

  • /pre-commitLab commandruns-commands

    Final gate before a commit - checks scope, debug output, secrets, stubs, skipped tests, and real test results. Ends with READY or NOT READY.

    Slop it targets
    Debug output, stubs, secrets, and skipped tests reaching a commit.
    Evidence you get back
    A checklist with evidence per line, then READY or NOT READY. Nothing is edited or committed.

    Read the prompt file: /pre-commit

  • /toolsBuilt-in

    Configure tools for a local chat.

    Turn off tools a task does not need, so the agent cannot wander into the terminal or the web.

    Example: /tools
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /tools

  • /hooksBuilt-in

    Configure hooks.

    Hooks enforce rules deterministically, which a prompt alone cannot.

    Example: /hooks
    Where: Local and Copilot · VS Code docs for /hooks

  • /create-hookBuilt-in

    Generate a hook in a local agent session.

    Adds a deterministic guardrail, such as running the tests after every edit.

    Example: /create-hook run npm test after file edits
    Where: Local agent session · VS Code docs for /create-hook

  • /disableAutoApproveBuilt-in

    Restore the default permission level. Alias: /disableYolo.

    Puts every edit and terminal command back behind your approval.

    Example: /disableAutoApprove
    Where: Local and Copilot CLI sessions · VS Code docs for /disableAutoApprove

  • /autoApproveBuilt-inCaution: removes a safety checkpoint

    Bypass tool approvals for the current session. Alias: /yolo.

    Listed so you can recognize it. It removes a safety checkpoint, so use it only in a disposable, sandboxed workspace.

    Example: /autoApprove
    Where: Local and Copilot CLI sessions · VS Code docs for /autoApprove

  • /sandboxBuilt-in

    /sandbox policy inspects the effective sandbox policy for a Copilot session.

    Shows what a sandboxed session may touch. Not available with Local.

    Example: /sandbox policy
    Where: Copilot sessions only - not Local · VS Code docs for /sandbox

Context Keep the context window clean.

Slop smell: Long chats drift, stale decisions leak into new work, and nobody can resume.

  • /handoffLab commandwrites-artifact

    Write HANDOFF.md - goal, state, decisions, evidence, open questions, next steps - so a fresh chat can continue without this one.

    Slop it targets
    Context rot and lost decisions between sessions.
    Evidence you get back
    A HANDOFF.md of at most 60 lines whose every path exists. Missing evidence says "not run".

    Read the prompt file: /handoff

  • /compactBuilt-in

    Compact conversation context.

    Summarizes earlier turns so stale detail stops crowding out the current task.

    Example: /compact
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /compact

  • /forkBuilt-in

    Fork the conversation with its history.

    Lets you try a risky alternative in a copy so the main thread stays clean.

    Example: /fork
    Where: Local. /fork <title> and /fork prompt <prompt> need an Agent Host session. · VS Code docs for /fork

  • /clearBuilt-in

    Start a new chat and archive or mark the current chat as done.

    Resets context between tasks. Pair it with /handoff so nothing important is lost.

    Example: /clear
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /clear

  • /renameBuilt-in

    Rename a local chat.

    Name sessions by task so you resume the right context instead of a random thread.

    Example: /rename csv-export refactor
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /rename

Diagnose and productivity Know what the agent saw and can do.

Slop smell: Guessing why a prompt, tool, or customization did not load.

  • /docBuilt-in

    Generate documentation comments from editor inline chat.

    Keeps docs next to the code they describe. Delete comments that only narrate the code.

    Example: /doc (in editor inline chat, with a function selected)
    Where: Editor inline chat · VS Code docs for /doc

  • /newBuilt-in

    Scaffold a workspace or file.

    Starts from a known template instead of a hand-rolled project layout.

    Example: /new node CLI with node:test
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /new

  • /newNotebookBuilt-in

    Scaffold a Jupyter notebook.

    Gives exploratory work a separate home, away from production code.

    Example: /newNotebook explore the orders CSV
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /newNotebook

  • /helpBuilt-in

    Shows what actually exists in this session instead of guessing.

    Example: /help
    Where: Local Ask chat · VS Code docs for /help

  • /modelsBuilt-in

    Open the model picker.

    Makes the model choice explicit and repeatable.

    Example: /models
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /models

  • /agentsBuilt-in

    Configure custom agents.

    Shows which agent personas exist and what tools they hold.

    Example: /agents
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /agents

  • /skillsBuilt-in

    Configure agent skills.

    Confirms which skills can load. See the sibling skills lab.

    Example: /skills
    Where: Local · VS Code docs for /skills

  • /promptsBuilt-in

    Configure prompt files.

    Where: Local and Copilot · VS Code docs for /prompts

  • /create-agentBuilt-in

    Generate a custom agent in a local agent session.

    Packages a role with a narrow tool list.

    Where: Local agent session · VS Code docs for /create-agent

  • /create-skillBuilt-in

  • /create-promptBuilt-in

    Generate a prompt file in a local agent session.

    Turns a good prompt you keep retyping into a reusable /command.

Also in the GitHub Copilot app

The GitHub Copilot app has its own slash commands, separate from VS Code. These are the anti-slop ones. This lab does not exercise them. Copilot app slash commands

  • /plan Switches to Plan mode.
  • /review Reviews the current session's changes.
  • /security-review Runs a security-focused review of current diffs.
  • /rubber-duck Asks a different model to critique your approach.
  • /spar Challenges your approach with adversarial reasoning.
  • /research Runs a research workflow and produces a cited report.
  • /context Shows the session's context usage.
  • /compact Summarizes earlier conversation to reduce token pressure.
  • /fork Forks the session at the latest turn.
  • /reset-allowed-tools Clears session tool approvals and turns auto-approval off.
  • /sandbox on Enables local sandboxing for the session.
  • /chronicle improve Suggests improvements to your instructions file.
